articleTitle: The Constraint Artificial-Intelligence Assisted Method for Etching Structure Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The artificial-intelligence (AI) assisted tuning method is explored for 3D NAND optimized etching structure throughout finding the suitable plasma etching parameters based on neural network deep learning in this study. The resulting plasma etching structure via AI assisted tuning shows comparable physical shape to that tuning from human domain. With the advanced collaboration of human domain and AI assisted tuning, a specific-purpose constraint AI assisted method brings forth the advantages of well-controlled etching architecture as well as defect saving that literally achieves a short turnaround time on problem-solving in the etching process of research and development.

articleTitle: Periphery Gate Optimization for Reducing Single-Sense Amp (SSA) Failure in DRAM: YE: Yield Enhancement/Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The paper presents a potent approach to enhancing front-end yield. It underscores a multifaceted issue that originates from various modules, illustrating the intricacy and significance of evaluating process interactions across layers. The paper showcases how a well-structured and data-driven problem-solving technique can effectively tackle a complex problem. This work lays the groundwork for enhancing other package-level testing issues and opens up further opportunities for process margin enhancement. It details the issue of misalignment between periphery gate contacts and the periphery gate for sense amplifiers. The problem intensifies when the underlying active area is larger, leading to the electrical shortening of the gate to source/drain contact. Alongside various efforts to improve the overlay, the issue was substantially mitigated by addressing it through gate length and contact target optimization, followed by a reticle edit for the active area at the failure location.

articleTitle: Effective Downsampling Techniques for SEM Defect Inspection Using Design Insights in Machine Learning: Topic/category: DI: Defect Inspection and Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: During wafer manufacturing, Bright Field Inspection (BFI) followed by SEM review is a widely used method for inline defect capture. Given the large number of defects reported by BFI, especially during R&D stage where the defectivity is often high, users need a way to effectively down sample the defects to be sent for SEM review. In this paper, we demonstrate various BFI to SEM down sampling techniques including, pattern-based clustering, and machine learning (ML) based down sampling that effectively find trends and make prediction to identify systematic weak patterns with increased SEM defect hit rate and systematic defect discovery.

articleTitle: Elimination of Bond Pad Etch Induced Wafer Arcing via Reducing ESC Chuck Surface Charges
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: DRAM wafers had frequent arcing events in a bond pad etch process, which resulted in severe yield loss, unscheduled down time, and associated cost due to part cleaning and replacement. The arcing was found to occur on wafers only at mirror position of upper I electrode pressure gauge port location. We have identified higher ESC chucking voltage and exposed Al at upper electrode as the main root causes for the arcing. A new baseline bond pad etch recipe with reduced ESC chucking/de-chucking voltage combined with a new recoating Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>coating procedure has been developed. With implementing this new baseline process, we have eliminated arcing events by 98%, improved unscheduled downtime of tools by 1.2% for maxing out production throughput, and reduced yield loss significantly.

articleTitle: Wet Etch Recipe Optimization for Enabling RMG Multi Vt Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Three chemistries are compared on metal oxide films to facilitate a stable and repeatable wet etching process to be used in the replacement metal gate module for multi-Vt for 2nm Gate All Around (GAA) Nanosheet. The etching recipes with the selected chemistry are optimized to improve within wafer (WiW) and wafer to wafer (WtW) uniformity using various chemical nozzle dispense options.

articleTitle: Metal Etch Depth Metrology using YieldStar and CDSEM
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In this work we demonstrate and report the capability of YieldStar and CDSEM to measure etch depths of metal in a data-driven approach. We find that both Yieldstar and CDSEM enable recess depth measurements with a precision of 0.5 nm over a range of 17 nm. Combining YieldStar and CDSEM (hybrid metrology) further improved prediction errors by 0.1 nm.

articleTitle: Process Control Solutions for GaN-on-Si Devices in a Production Line
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Our paper will present defect control solutions for manufacturing Gallium Nitride (GaN) devices in a silicon production line. The flexibility of defect inspection and review tools allowed us to successfully implement a full defectivity control plan for both silicon and GaN-on-Si wafers. In addition, two novel methods were employed for the detection of a GaN-specific defect. First, SEM review equipment was used as an inspection tool to detect and enumerate the number of killer defects and second, the intensity output of an inspection system was utilized for high-speed mapping of the overall defectivity on a wafer.

articleTitle: Rapid Analysis of Organic Contaminants in Semiconductor Process Chemicals and on Wafer Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: We have developed instrumentation to measure trace levels of organic contaminants in process chemicals and solvents used in semiconductor fabrication as well as organic contaminants in the residue that can be left behind on the surface of a semiconductor wafer. The instrument combines the high sensitivity detection of Electrospray Ionization (ESI) and accurate mass determination of Time of Flight Mass Spectrometer (TOF-MS) with advanced automation to enable the real time detection of trace organics. Detection limits in the low parts per trillion(ppt) can be achieved for detecting organic contaminants in process chemicals. For measuring organic contamination on wafer surfaces scanning technique like VPD analysis is used and detection limits of ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> molecules/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> can be achieved. This accomplishment meets the critical challenges related to analysis of organic contaminants outlined in the 2023 IRDS roadmap.

articleTitle: An Innovative Method and Apparatus for KGSD Testing of 2.5D and 3D Stacked Dies, with Emphasis on High Bandwidth Memory (HBM)
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: A novel method and associated apparatus tailored for the KGD testing of 2.5D and 3D stacked dies, particularly focusing on High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) have been developed. This is important because the distinctive architecture of HBM necessitates the compression of I/O contacts into a limited, confined space, posing challenges for conventional probing techniques at the die level. To address this issue, we propose a methodology employing vision-based alignment and vacuumpressured chuck, enabling precise positioning of test probes relative to the contact pads of the device under test.

articleTitle: Predictive Analysis and Root Cause Identification of Equipment Failures Using Event Log Patterns: A Focus on EUV/DUV Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving field of semiconductor manufacturing, the productivity and reliability of advanced semiconductor equipment, especially Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) and Deep Ultraviolet (DUV) lithography systems, are of paramount importance. This research introduces a cutting-edge methodology that employs the analysis of the rarity of event logs to preemptively identify potential failures and their root causes within such equipment. By establishing an optimized threshold that delineates the normal from the rare, this approach effectively flags those rare logs that exceed this threshold as indicators of potential failures. Subsequent analysis of these logs reveals the underlying mechanisms of failure, allowing for timely intervention. The application of this methodology to EUV/DUV equipment has demonstrated a significant increase in predictive accuracy, with a recall of 97.6%, and the potential to realize annual savings of nearly $2 million by reducing equipment downtime and maintenance costs.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Trace-SPC Anomaly Detection Solution Based on VAE Model
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Wafer manufacturing is a complex, expensive, and time-consuming process that involves multiple steps. By closely monitoring the corresponding variations in process parameters, potential anomalies and faults in the process can be timely detected and identified, effectively improving equipment utilization and product yield. However, the anomaly detection methods currently in use rely on extracting feature values from sensor data and analyzing the statistical information of these features. This approach fails to identify complex anomaly patterns, and constructing meaningful feature values can be challenging. In this paper, we propose an unsupervised anomaly detection solution based on the Variational Autoencoder (VAE) model. We optimized the training strategy of the VAE model to address the issue of posterior collapse. By reconstructing the sensor data using the VAE model, we can effectively convert anomalous patterns into normal ones. The experimental results confirm the effectiveness of the model across various sensor datasets, demonstrating the capability of the proposed solution to accurately identify abnormal patterns within the sensor data.

articleTitle: Defect Reduction And Line Width Roughness (LWR) improvement By Using A Post Precoat Treatment (PPT) In Waferless Chamber Conditioning (WCC)
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Defect and line width roughness are two main yield detractors in advanced bitline dry etch process in high-volume DRAM memory manufacturing. In this paper, we present the results of defect reduction and LWR improvement by using a Post Pre-coat Treatment method in Waferless Chamber Clean recipe. Adding a PPT step at the end of WCC recipe reduces defect, inline critical dimension (CD) and LWR. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) results show pre-coat silicon oxide and/or PPT improves surface roughness by 30%. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) has been utilized to characterize the surfaces treated with and without PPT, indicating PPT can remove residue chloride and solidify SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> film from its loose form. With the implementation of WCC with PPT, we have achieved 0.15% yield gain which is resulted from defect reduction, tighter inline CD and LWR improvement.

articleTitle: Fault Detection of Wafer Sensors Based on Representation Learning and Isolation Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Wafer manufacturing is a complex process involving hundreds of process steps. Detecting and identifying potential anomalies and malfunctions in sensor parameters are crucial for improving production yield. However, traditional rule-based or statistical methods fail to meet the requirements of accuracy and efficiency. To address this issue, we propose an innovative model that combines deep learning with Isolation Forest. The deep learning module is used to extract multi-dimensional feature vectors at each timestamp, while the Isolation Forest module takes the multi-dimensional feature vectors at each timestamp as input for anomaly detection in the timestamp dimension. We conducted experiments using a real industrial dataset and compared our model with several state-of-the-art models. The results demonstrate that our model exhibits strong learning and representation capabilities, enabling it to learn from large amounts of data and identify complex anomaly patterns.

articleTitle: Difference Image-Based Training Sets for Automatic Defect Classification at Outgoing Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Outgoing quality control/assurance (OQA) and defect inspection in the semiconductor industry is of utmost importance in the realm of high-volume manufacturing. Finished wafers exiting an integrated circuit (IC) fabrication facility frequently demand a high rate of inspection to ensure outgoing quality. The intent of outgoing quality inspection is to ensure that reliable and functional chips are manufactured. When establishing an effective outgoing quality system, both to prevent financial loss from return material authorization and to enable effective and timely investigation into defect issues, the accurate classification of defectivity is paramount. This paper proposes to construct an enhanced (augmented) training set based on defect-reference difference images, rather than the direct use of the defect image, in a machine learning model for classifying defects at outgoing inspection. The model using the enhanced dataset proves to have more accurate classification for critical defectivity. The proposed methodology of augmenting the training data resulted in a model with an overall recall of 88.8%, more than a 4% improvement from using only the defect image to train the model; further, the weighted precision shows an almost 5% increase using the proposed methodology. It is presumed that the enhanced dataset has a stronger capability of predicting defect characteristics by reducing background noise.

articleTitle: Lithography WEE, EBR and Pre-SiGe HF Clean Flow Rate Optimization for Wafer Edge Defectivity Improvement
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Defects on wafers have always been a major concern in wafer fabrication processing. Most defect optimization activities centered around improving wafer front side defects by having more-clean steps, process chamber controls, process recipe improvements etc. However, there is minimum focus and attention on wafer edge bevel defects due to the lack of suitable equipment and detection methods and lack of skills and knowledge about their origin and effects. These defects can impact yield performance, cause wafer scrap, and even impact equipment uptime and higher costs due to machine faults and reworks. Often a series of cleaning and defect scanning equipment is needed that can easily cause a day or two days loss of cycle time. In this paper, we focus on how the defects are transported to the wafer frontside from the wafer's edge bevel and a provide a new understanding on how to reduce wafer edge defects from the wafer bevel by focusing on the process steps that cause defect formation.

articleTitle: Process and Tool Monitoring Strategy for Advanced Magnetic Tunnel Junction Stack Deposition
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper will present the method by which a magnetron physical vapor deposition (PVD) tool is monitored and controlled for purposes of depositing a Magnetic Tunnel Junction (MTJ) stack in a research and prototyping fab environment. The fabricated MTJ stack is utilized as an integral component of a Magnetoresistive Random Access Memory (MRAM) device and as such, stringent control of layer characteristics and dimension is critical to the performance of the overall device [1]. In this paper, the structure and deposition process of a MTJ stack will be briefly discussed in relation to key tool parametrics and wafer monitoring strategies. In addition, the paper will examine case studies showing the detection and containment of potential excursion events utilizing the presented monitoring strategies.

articleTitle: Feed-Forward Run-to-Run Process Control Based on Device Array Density for LPCVD Furnace Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Furnace LPCVD processes have been used in Semiconductor Industry to enable high aspect ratio film deposition and for high throughput through batching of multiple lots and wafers in a single batch. Any typical wafer process will have varying levels aspect ratios or topography and each technology node will involve different device array densities due to different customer requirements. The high aspect ratio surface topography creates loading effect in the furnace that will cause thickness variation depending on the array density. This causes thickness variation when batching different density Product together. This loading effect also creates a need to segregate different array density wafers into unique processes with different levels of tuning to achieve good thickness control. But this segregation is not efficient in high volume manufacturing due to batch size limitations. In this paper, we have presented a new feed forward R2R control method based on device array density that improves thickness performance even with different density product batched together which consequently improves yield and reduces cost of operation through better throughput.

articleTitle: Elimination of Pinhole Defects in Self-Aligned Double Patterning Process by using Bias Pulsed Plasma
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Self-aligned double patterning (SADP) is extensively utilized in advanced sub-20nm technology nodes. The DRAM digit contact SADP dry etch process experienced severe yield loss due to pinhole defects in the periphery. The root cause was identified through etching characteristics analysis to be the micro-loading effect between the dense/isolated areas and non-uniform etching from center-to-edge of the wafer. Using the design of experiment model, a new recipe has been developed to eliminate pinhole defects by optimizing bias pulsing and pressure. This approach has led to a 50% improvement in etching uniformity and better etching selectivity. The proposed recipe has effectively eliminated pinhole formation, significant improving pinhole-related yield loss from 0.3%-50% to zero.

articleTitle: 12LP FinFET CMOS Ultra-Low Leakage SRAM Devices with 0.54pA/cell Istby
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Low power device with ultra-low leakage (ULL) is the mainstream for current and future nano Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) memory devices. In addition, leakage power reduction during data-retention mode in Static random-access memory (SRAM) standby needs to be significantly improved with reduced supply voltage. In this paper, ULL SRAM designed on GlobalFoundries 12LP CMOS technology is presented. Achieving a record low device level retention standby leakage of 0.54pA/cell, together with −20% Vtsat mismatch reduction and +10%/+12% n/pSRAM performance boost. In addition, cross wafer uniformity of SRAM standby leakage has been reviewed with −35% within-wafer (WiW) improvement.

articleTitle: Strategies to Attract the Next Generation of Talent to the Semiconductor Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The semiconductor industry is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 12.28% from 2023 to 2032 which necessitates an enlarged workforce. In this paper, we present findings on strategies to attract the next generation of talent, with emphasis on increasing the participation of women within the semiconductor industry and opening the talent pipeline beyond electrical and computer engineering. Another key opportunity is for the industry to increase and highlight its contributions towards the common good-including social responsibility with an emphasis on environmental impact-to capture the interest of students.

articleTitle: Protocol for Thermal Donors Monitoring in High Resistivity Silicon Wafers
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: A monitoring protocol for 300mm high-resistivity Czochralski silicon (Cz-Si) wafers after optimized thermal treatments, is presented. It is based on the combination of several metrology techniques. Having such a methodology is important as oxygen-related defects called Thermal Donors (TD) formed during 450°C anneals are electrically active in various types of substrates: n-type used typically in InsulatedGate Bipolar Transistors (IGBT) and p-type used for example in Radiofrequency (RF)-based technologies. We show that such TDs result in resistivity loss, confirming their detrimental impact on devices performances.

articleTitle: DTCO Guided Process Integration: Case Studies From FEOL & BEOL with BSPDN Topic: DTCO/DFM
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: We present two case studies where Design Technology Co-Optimization (DTCO) methodology can aid in down-selection of integration options unique to back side power distribution network (BSPDN) implementation. In the FEOL, co-integration of Front to Back Via (FBV) with gate-cut (CT) integration schemes need to balance performance and area scaling tradeoffs. Design considerations for FBV for both CT first and CT last schemes are discussed with process variation estimations and self-alignment schemes. In BEOL, opportunistic aspect ratio optimization of frontside metal interconnect stacks capability to offer greater heat dissipation capability without adversely impacting performance is discussed. A design point with a line/space/stack height combination of BEOL metal stack to optimize RC delay is proposed alongside a thermal resistance circuit modeling methodology to assess heat dissipation is also reviewed. (Abstract)

articleTitle: TEOS Integrated High-Low Pressure RPS Clean: APC: Advanced Process Control
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Current clean recipe settings utilize high-pressure values referencing best-known methods (BKM) for remote plasma chamber NF3 cleaning. In this paper, a novel cleaning recipe integrating high and low pressure values is demonstrated. The working mechanism of this improved cleaning is explained through the concept of mean free path, where the addition of a lower pressure cleaning step enables ionized fluorine radicals to travel longer before collision and covering a wider area, serving as a complement to high pressure cleaning. This novel chamber cleaning procedure with two consecutive clean steps: initial high pressure step followed by a low pressure step has been evaluated in an industrial PECVD chamber, showing up to 60% reduction in particle counts, 8.5% reduction in Ar and NF3 usage and gas cost savings.

articleTitle: Deploying an Advanced Scheduling Solution to Optimize Conflicting KPIs in the Diffusion Area at Renesas Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This work focuses on the scheduling of the diffusion area at a Renesas fab. Scheduling the diffusion area of a front-end wafer fab is significantly challenging due to batching, re-entrant flows, and complex timelink constraints. We present an advanced scheduling solution that optimizes batching, tool allocation, batch launch times, timelink violations along with other operational constraints in the fab, aligning with Renesas' goal of making the best possible trade-offs between competing objectives. The developed method has been deployed in Renesas production lines. Results show significant increase in diffusion batching efficiency by up to 27% and a substantial decrease of timelink violations by up to 54%.

articleTitle: Thickness Description of Thick GaN Film Stack and Measurement of Al Percentage in AlGaN Alloy with KLA SpectraShape™ 10K
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Broadband spectroscopic ellipsometry (BBSE) has been successfully used to characterize and measure layer thicknesses in complex GaN/AIGaN/Ainfilm stacks using the KLA SpectraShape 10K dimensional metrology system. With a parametric oscillator model for the AlxGal-xN alloy dispersion, the dependence of the alloy bandgap from the Aluminum concentration was tracked and compared to reference photoluminescence (PL) data. A correlation table was created using a quadratic relation allowing for immediate measurement of the Al concentration directly on the SpectraShape 10K tool.

articleTitle: Development of Epitaxial SiGeB as a Test Vehicle to Evaluate Source-Drain Etchout During Channel Release of Gate-all-Around Devices: Topic/category: AEPM: Advanced Equipment Processes and Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Nanosheet (NS) gate-all-around (GAA) technology will be replacing finFET devices due to improved device performance and area scaling [1]. A significant challenge in NS GAA technology is etchout (EO) of the source/drain (S/D) EPI during channel release (CR). Optimizing inner spacer (IS) shape and thickness and CR chemistry are some of the key factors required to eliminate EO. To characterize the mechanisms driving EO and quickly identify and solutions require a short loop (SL) test vehicle that is susceptible to EO. Our traditional pFET SL that is used for structural and electrical evaluation of NS GAA devices used SiB S/D epi, which is not susceptible to EO due to the high selectivity of the CR chemistry to SiB. SiGeB is easily etched by CR chemistry. Therefore, it was necessary for us to develop a SL with SiGeB S/D in order to evaluate EO. We developed a selective epitaxial SiGeB process with good structural integrity that showed large performance increase over our traditional SiB-based SL, providing a good test vehicle for evaluating and improving EO. We characterized the structural and electrical properties of this process with various techniques. Finally, we used this SL to identify which CR chemistries had the best etchout performance.

articleTitle: A Case of Plasma-Induced Film Breakdown in 3D NAND BEOL Dielectric Etch
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In the latest 3D NAND product development, top via hole etch process is almost the last hole connecting process to complete a device fabrication. However, we encountered severe film damaged defects leading to a loss of over 30% in yield. Through a series of analyses, we uncovered the underlying root cause that relates to the presence of extensive metal defects embedded beneath the layer of inter-metal dielectric (IMD). As via hole etching down through IMD, unexpectedly arcing was happened because of overcharging onto these floating metal defects in plasma. This phenomenon has had a detrimental impact on process stability and yield. This paper comprehensively reports the mechanisms of defect formation and film breakdown damage on the structure. We also propose a solution to mitigate the problem and recover the yield effectively.

articleTitle: Surface Leakage of Zener Diode and Its Degradation Behaviour due to Diminishing Field Effect Passivation
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the PN junction reversed leakage current of zener diode attributed to the surface recombination, and the drift behavior after reliability stress. The leakage current before stress can be correlated to the charges from a silicon nitride process which can be modulated by the film thickness. The degradation mechanism after Bias Temperature Stress due to the diminishing the field effect passivation by positive charges from silicon nitride process are discussed and illustrated in this paper.

articleTitle: Optimization of O2 Plasma After Silicon Etch Process to Prevent Br-Induced Equipment Corrosion and Pattern Abnormality
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Although hydrogen bromide (HBr) is an effective silicon etchant for patterning, it also generates SiBrx as a contaminant that causes equipment corrosion in the presence of moisture. We can apply O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma post-etch treatment (PET) to remove this, while it also comes with the risk of triggering abnormal etch profile. As balancing this trade-off relationship by optimizing settings of O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> PET is essential, our research revealed the behaviors of Br and O on wafers exposed to various O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma conditions, leading to the determination of optimal O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> PET settings with 2.5 to 5 percent of oxygen gas composition.

articleTitle: Hafnium Chloride Pulse Time Reduction on Atomic Layer Deposited High-K HfO2 Dielectric Films
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: For Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) in high volume manufacturing, higher pulse time for the precursor causes waste of chemical when similar deposition thickness can be achieved with reduced pulse time. Higher pulse time also leads to thicker deposition on the chamber walls and susceptor edges of the reaction chamber causing impact to chamber lifetime and leading to early chamber kit changes. In this study, we are depositing Hf02 using ALD technique and studying the impact of variation in pulse time of the HfCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>(precursor) on film thickness, percent Hf, percent O, dielectric constant and device performance. We are also studying the impact of HfCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> purge time, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O (oxidant) pulse and purge times on Hf02 film thickness. These process modulations help in understanding the reaction mechanism of HfCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>/H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O ALD process better. By implementing a lower pulse time for this process in high volume manufacturing, higher throughput can be achieved. Other benefits will be improved chamber lifetime and longer chemical lifetime.

articleTitle: Controlling Discharge Condition of PE-SION Deposition Process for Finding a Balance Between NH3 Outgassing and Surface-Remained NH4+ions
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In this work, the ability of reducing reaction byproduct from chemical vapor deposition of SiON thin film is explored changing balance gas, time and power within the wafer discharging process. In order to control the surface remaining NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>byproduct, which is reported to induce profile deviation in photolithography patterning, post N2O plasma treatment has been widely used. However, the N2O plasma treatment has inherent limitation of utilizing greenhouse gas and imperfect removal efficiency. Although N2 is generally considered to be inert due to the stable triple N-N bond, based on the material screening and DFT calculation, we newly postulated that N* radical from N2 plasma may reduce NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>ions more efficiently compared with O* radical from N2O plasma, possibly by the more favored H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>dissociation reaction between NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and NH3 (-32.6 eV for N* radical driven pathway / −21.9 eV for O* radical driven pathway). Indeed, by using slight plasma power generated during the wafer discharging stage and changing balance gas from N2O to N2, the surface remaining NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>ion was removed by almost 100% confirmed by High Performance Ion Chromatography (HPIC). Additionally, critical dimension uniformity of EUV patterning was also improved by 0.03nm in ADI and 0.11nm in ACI states, respectively. We believe that our finding exploits new strategy for controlling surface condition of hard mask with more simplified and sustainable method.

articleTitle: Cloud Big Data Lake for Advanced Analytics in Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Data driven business intelligence is changing how semiconductor manufacturing thrives in the long term. A cloud big data lake is designed and implemented based on state-of-the-art cloud architecture providing complete services for data ingestion, storage, processing, advanced analytics, and machine learning with a high level of security. Efficient and effective use of this big data lake and data science enables problem solving and decision making to improve productivity and performance.

articleTitle: Real-Time Water Leak Detection and Preventing Yield Excursions in Lithography
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Cooling water is extensively used in photolithography for temperature control of coating and developing[1]. Water leaks can cause failure in semiconductor manufacturing processes [2], resulting in significant wafer yield loss. Inspecting or replacing all water jackets periodically is time- consuming and costly. Due to a rapid flow of cooling water running at 5l/min in TEL Track [3], it is hard to detect bubbles in the TCU (temperature control unit) return line by ordinary bubble detection methods readily available on the market. A photoelectric sensor with a retro-reflective type can be used to detect high-speed liquid or bubbles in specific applications. When an object, such as a liquid or bubble, passes through the beam of light, the amount of light reflected in the sensor changes, which can trigger an output signal. This paper will present a cost- effective setup of fiber optic evanescent sensors for early detection of water jackets or tubing cracks to eliminate the risk of wafer defects due to potential liquid leaks.

articleTitle: Feedback Control in Station Dispatching to Improve Constraint Tool Output in 300mm Fabs
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: We present a novel feedback control system which influences wafer Lot prioritization over multiple non-constraint steps leading to a constraint toolset, improving the constraint's output. The results of deployment at Intel's high-volume manufacturing fabs show output improvements of up to 16% at Photo-lithography Scanners. The benefit demonstrated is especially significant given that it did not involve any new hardware, and the software development was minimal. This system is not Photo-lithography specific; it can be used for any fab constraint toolset enabling increased output by strategic feeding of the constraint.

articleTitle: Optimizing High-Product-Mix Manufacturing with Advanced Process Control through Machine Learning-Based Virtual Metrology
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The semiconductor foundry encounters challenges in addressing multifaceted customer requirements and complicated manufacturing procedures. Variations within the chemical vapor deposition (CVD) process directly impact transistor characteristics and overall yield. Advanced machine learning (ML) software gives rise to an extended virtual metrology (VM) model enhanced by design feature and real-time fault detection and classification (FDC) data. Through the integration of an advanced process control (APC) system, the manufacturing process effectively mitigates film thickness variations within high-product-mix foundry fabs. This remarkable outcome is validated through control simulations.

articleTitle: Using Monte Carlo Simulation - a Predictive Model to Identify Capacity and Cycle Time Detractors in a Semiconductor Foundry
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing (fab) is a complex and precise industry. On top of that, the industry is extremely high cost, so it is crucial to get as accurate as possible when planning the Fab's capacity. However, due to the nature of the industry there are many dynamic factors that play a role in capacity planning that are hard to model into one precise capacity model. In this paper, we proposed to use Monte Carlo Method to simulate the Fab performance and provide a quick high-level prediction of possible performance detractors affecting Fab output. This can help to plan for more support on areas that are predicted to be uncertain/risky. Overall, this simulation can help guide to better decision making and protect Fab output commitments.

articleTitle: Impact of Implantation Conditions on the In-Depth Distribution of Implanted Species in SiC and GaN
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Seen as vectors for reducing energy consumption, power electronic components for wide-bandgap semiconductors (SiC, GaN…) play a strategic role in the electric mobility and power conversion sector. The proposed paper will present the results of a collaboration between IBS and CAMECA illustrating the effect of different implantation conditions (energy, angle, dose, temperature) on the in-depth distribution of implanted species.

articleTitle: Critical Defect Detection at 3nm Technology Node: Enhanced Detection Using DUV Optical Inspection Technology With AI-Based Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In this paper, we present the results of a study conducted using cutting-edge deep-ultraviolet (DUV) brightfield wafer inspection technology, enhanced by a new artificial intelligence (AI) based image enhancer algorithm. The study focused on the most advanced design rule technology and demonstrated a reduction of up to 2.8x in the number of defects that are sent for Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) review, while maintaining an equal or better Capture Rate of key Defects of Interest (DOI) compared to the benchmark inspection recipe. These results highlight the potential value of the AI-based algorithm in achieving tighter defect control and enabling higher yield, all while minimizing the Fab Cost of Ownership.

articleTitle: Copper Electromigration Improvement Through Aluminum Barrier and Related Process Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Electromigration (EM) failure is one of the major concerns for back-end-of-line (BEOL) with Cu interconnects. Many factors contribute to Cu EM failure. Study shows Cu Al barrier, and the related process has a significant role in managing Cu EM issue in the thick Cu process. In this paper, we reviewed possible EM failure mechanisms and, a significant improvement of EM lifetime is achieved for a thick Cu process by optimization of Al barrier and related processes.

articleTitle: Double-Edged Effect of Aqueous Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) on Silicon Interface Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: RCA (Radio Corporation of America) clean remains as one of the most prevalent cleaning schemes in semiconductor manufacturing ever since it was developed by Kern in the 1960s [1], [2]. A plethora of studies have affirmed the cleaning mechanism and effectiveness of SC1 & SC2 in removing organic and metallic impurities from the wafer surface. However, less emphasis was placed on investigating the interplay between RCA cleaning sequence with the silicon surface reaction at the interface in the aqueous HF (hydrofluoric acid). In this interesting work, some compelling findings observed during our study to improve the wafer-edge yield at the top quadrant on 0.13um BiCMOS wafers are presented. Our analysis unveiled the predominance of “HF -last” in the cavity RCA clean and its immersion time effect when coupled with the interaction of SC2 on the silicon interface. A remarkable breakthrough was then demonstrated invariably in the wafer-edge performance by skipping SC2 compounded with a shorter “HF -last” immersion time. These insights not only brought in an innovative process sequence optimization, which had proclaimed an astounding wafer-edge yield improvement, but also food for thought on processes in which the interface quality poses a concern for the downstream integration. Our work is also reckoned to eventually lead to cost and chemical waste reduction in response to environmental sustainability.

articleTitle: Consideration of a Ga-FIB in Lamella Sample Prep for EBIC Analysis of Advanced-node SRAMs
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: An experiment to understand possible detrimental effects from processing SRAM samples with gallium focused ion beams (Ga-FIB) prior to electron beam induced current (EBIC) characterization is presented. To understand the magnitude of sample surface amorphization upon the ability to collect EBIC measurements, a lamella was prepared with different areas of increasingly improved polish, followed by EBIC measurements at 1 and 2 kV beam landing energy. The results indicate that EBIC measurements on a 5 nm SRAM lamella are minimally impacted by variations in final FIB polishing optimization, a reminder that these measurements are interacting with a volume in the sample, rather than merely the surface. A second experiment showed the ability to perform high-magnification EBIC measurements underneath gates.

articleTitle: In-Situ Post Etch Fluorocarbon Byproduct Removal for HDP Void Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: DRAM Recessed Access Device (RAD) module is impacted by Cap oxide voids that causes yield impact through broken wordline. The Cap oxide is the high-density plasma (HDP) oxide that caps the metal wordline. This failure is correlated to queue time at RAD Cap Oxide Dep (HDP) from the incoming clean step, with higher wait time (queue time or qtime) causing fails. The fails are also heavily impacting slot 25 in the FOUP with a unique wafer shading while remaining wafer slots have an edge of the wafer shading. The interaction of the FOUP with the wafers was analyzed through Airborne molecular contamination (AMC) measurements. High Acids and HF AMC were observed post Etch and Strip. Oxide etch uses C4F6/Ar/O2 plasma for selective Oxide etch. This selective etch relies on high fluorocarbon deposition for selectivity. An insitu post etch treatment (PET) with Oxygen plasma is presented in this paper to remove the fluorocarbons in the etch chamber itself to minimize byproduct outgassing into the FOUP inner walls which prevents further interaction of byproduct from the FOUP downstream causing the voids.

articleTitle: Auto Furnace Scheduler with Built in Timelink Regulator (Auto Kitter)
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Inwafer fab manufacturing, furnace process requires robust planning not only to optimize the overall equipment efficiency but also to ensure quality in terms of timelink between wet benches and furnaces, especially in a 200mm manual fab. Knowledge and experience play critical roles in furnaces dispatching. Thus, it becomes a highly human dependent process. A team was formed with the objective of eliminating the dependency on humans and improving the productivity and quality of furnace operation. A smart and comprehensive dispatching logic has been established by modelling the knowledge and skills developed through the years into a system named Auto Kitter, which consists of batching assignment at tool level, time link control at wet benches and at the same time, it incorporates with tool constraints and scheduled activities.

articleTitle: An Implementation of a Machine Learning Methodology for Improving Test Data Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: A Machine Learning methodology has been developed to successfully improve the test data quality by identifying outliers for validation of potential testing related issues. This ensures a fast turnaround time with limited test resources.

articleTitle: Die-Level Serialization Platform Demonstration
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The semiconductor industry is lacking a solution for unique die-level labeling that is economical and compatible with volume manufacturing. Laser-based lithography has lower throughput compared to standard photolithography process however for low volume foundries and laboratories already owning one, it is the shortest path to serialization. The DIGITHO die-serialization platform is compatible with such equipment offering a solution for die-level serialization of low throughput manufacturing.

articleTitle: Combining Batchspray and Ozone Reduces Chemical Consumption in Wafer Cleaning
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Sustainability has become a goal for the global economy, society, technology, and manufacturing including semiconductor fabs. The use of ozone for cleaning applications perfectly supports sustainability programs within semiconductor manufacturing. High throughput, minimum media consumption, and repeatable performance are just a few benefits of batch spray cleaning technology that incorporates the sicOzone process. Additionally, spiking technology combined with ozone results in comparable cleanliness compared to traditional cleaning methods. We present results showing particle levels, cleaning efficiency, metal contamination, oxide loss and uniformity.

articleTitle: Design Modification to Mitigate Ethylene Glycol Corrosion Risk in Dry Etching Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Plasma dry etch is used to produce small structures in semiconductor devices. To achieve precise, selective, and controlled etching results, effective temperature control must be maintained in plasma etch machines. Ethylene glycol (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>OH)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>is a desirable coolant for temperature control in various dry etching machines. Despite its chemical properties such as its ability to maintain heat transfer effectiveness in high temperature and high-pressure environment, ethylene glycol poses corrosion risk to metallic parts of machines. Continuous channels were created through modification of corner plates on dry etch machines to mitigate corrosion risk from glycol. Significant reductions in coolant leakage and environmental contamination were observed.

articleTitle: ScCO2 Drying for Preventing Pattern Collapse in Advanced Logic Device Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Supercritical CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (ScCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) drying has been demonstrated to prevent pattern collapse causing Line Flop-over (LF) during post gate reactive ion etching (RIE) cleaning of advanced Nanosheet devices. Drying with conventional low surface tension liquids like IPA did not help in preventing the LF's in these high aspect ratio structures (AR = 13–17).

articleTitle: Scheduling Semiconductor Manufacturing Operations in Research and Development Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper focuses on a scheduling problem encountered in shop floors of Research and Development (R&D) semiconductor manufacturing facilities. R&D facilities are characterized by a large product mix in very small quantities with unique/non-standard/varying processing routes, little process control of engineering experiments, dynamic prioritization of research activities, and pre-process checks. In contrast to typical scheduling problems found in semiconductor manufacturing systems, we provide and discuss the implications of factors of complexity (unknown parameters, evolving settings, R&D fab characteristics, etc.) on operations' scheduling specific to R&D environments. An existing dispatching rule-based heuristic, running in R&D settings, is challenged, investigated, and improved. Numerical experiments are conducted on a real-life instance and analyzed in terms of: (i) the sequence performance and quality, and (ii) the approximation accuracy of uncertain processing times and its impact on the decision performance.

articleTitle: UPC Fault Reduction via CPEC Backside Surface Roughness Control
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Direct exposure to high frequency radio frequency (HF RF) by the electrostatic chuck (ESC) leads to permanent damage to the ESC surface, which results in a process shift or clamping reliability problem. It is necessary to protect ESC during chamber cleaning and conditioning. This is done by covering the chuck with clampable protective ESC cover (CPEC). In this study, CPESs were prepared to study the impact of backside surface roughness towards universal pressure controller (UPC) fault, where the fault is a result of improper clamping that arise by leakage of backside cooling helium gas to the process chamber. Backside average roughness (Ra) for CPEC was measured at the outer edge. Ra values were collected, and it was found that covers with high backside Ra values lead to backside helium leakage and thus resulted in UPC faults during precoat deposition process. Fault trend data was collected for 5 consecutive months. It was observed that once backside Ra values of covers were controlled to a value no exceeding UPC fault rate dropped by 90% on the monitored tools. In general, low Ra is critical to prevent the UPC faults during precoat deposition process, with a corresponding reduction in tool downtime.

articleTitle: ASMC: Improving Measurement Data Quality with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper covers the methodology to identify Erroneous data when partial ground truth is available. Random Forest would be trained from the identified Erroneous data, and model is able to achieve a 97% True Expected data after retest of Erroneous data.

articleTitle: Real-Time Balancing of WIP for Compatible Capacities Across Distant Fab Buildings Using Automated Cross-Location Decisions
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The paper will discuss an automated decision approach that was employed at a multi-building Fab during a ramp-up phase to balance compatible capacities in two buildings of the Fab. The two buildings are situated at some distance from each other and not integrated with an Automated Material Handling System (AMHS); hence, Work In Process (WIP) movement has to be decided in a very careful manner. The paper will discuss the decision challenges involved, possible solution approaches, and the chosen solution with results.

articleTitle: Reliable Cu Pillar Undercut Control Using the Endpoint Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper addresses the key challenges of copper (Cu) undercut control using the end point detection (EPD) system based on the Applied Materials Raider tool. The Cu etch rate was measured with the timed etch to validate the end point detection on blanket wafers. The end point traces were then collected on C4 pillars under 0, 25, 50, and 100% over etch conditions. C4 pillars undercut amounts were measured using Focused Ion Beam Scanning Electron Microscopy (FIB-SEM). The ability to detect the endpoint (EP) and stop at a defined over etch (OE) from the end point was demonstrated. Based on FIB-SEM and Energy dispersive X-ray (EDX), we have developed an endpoint recipe with minimal undercut.

articleTitle: Autonomous Robot Orchestration Solution for OHT with Machine Learning and Digital Twin FA: Factory Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Autonomous Robot Orchestration Solution (AROS) is revolutionizing robot fleet management. AROS identifies the state and environment of each robot and enables them to achieve common goals collaboratively. In this paper, we introduce AROS and its application in controlling massive Overhead Hoist Transport (OHT) vehicles in semiconductor fabs. Key technologies in AROS include reinforcement learning algorithms and deep auto- encoder models. Digital Twin (DT) replicates the real system in a virtual environment with real-time communication to enhance decision-making for OHTs. We demonstrate the positive impact of AROS on OHT system performance, reducing average delivery times and increasing delivery capacity. AROS anomaly detection algorithm and health monitoring solution handle unexpected errors. This eliminates the need for human intervention. Our findings are supported by real use cases in large-scale semicon- durtor fabs.

articleTitle: A Particle Reduction Strategy for Plasma Etching Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Random defects caused by “fallen” particles in plasma etch processes have had a chronically detrimental impact on chip product yield. In this study, we conducted a vertical structure analysis of a particle defect and a process partition test methodology to accurately identify the various factors and the points of occurrence of the defects in the complex plasma etch processes. The root cause of particle contamination was identified as being related to the loss of electrostatic force during each processing sub-stage. Based on these findings, a comprehensive particle reduction strategy was devised, customized to each specific case. By exploiting the phenomenon of particle entrapment around the plasma sheath boundary, it was possible to effectively control particle contamination prior to the commencement of the main etch, during the substage etch transition phases, and after the final over-etch step. In addition, the implementation of an O2-based post-plasma treatment (PET) technique was also found to alleviate the byproduct-induced defect that reacted with moisture present in the cleanroom air.

articleTitle: First Results from a New Online Nano Liquid Particle Monitor on Ultra-Pure Water
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents initial results from new nano liquid particle monitoring technology for evaluating ultrapure water (UPW), which addresses a critical need in the industry to measure concentrations of colloidal particles below ~30 nm. The system combines UPW aerosolization/drying and water-based condensation particle counting to detect colloidal particles above a threshold size, ~10 nm in this work, while largely excluding much smaller residue particles arising from dissolved content. Results from extended use on two UPW systems, including one at a major semiconductor manufacturing foundry, demonstrate key performance attributes needed for a successful online monitoring system. These include clear settling to baseline, matched performance of multiple units in parallel, ability to distinguish between water qualities at different points in a polish process, long-term stability over multiple weeks of continuous use, ability to monitor the gradual rinse-down of replacement ion exchange resins in mixed beds, and the sensitive detection of breakthrough. Linear response to relevant nanoparticle concentrations is demonstrated by injections of different dilutions of monodispersed colloidal silica ranging from ~10 to ~60 nm diameter.

articleTitle: Advanced Metrology of Thick Silicon Nitride Films at 300 mm Scale for Next Generation High-Q Photonic Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The proposed paper will present various inline and offline advanced metrology data of thick SiN films (~>500 nm) prepared by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) and low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (LPCVD) techniques. Our study combines high-volume inline and high-accuracy offline metrology to best characterize our thick SiN films. We present a refractive index (n) comparison for annealed and unannealed PECVD/LPCVD wafers.

articleTitle: Data Variability Study of Advanced 3D NAND Memory using Python
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The methodology for data analysis with large variability based on Python is discussed and demonstrated. As NAND memory transitioned from 2D to 3D, a significant new source of variability emerged due to the stacking of several hundred layers of memory cells on top of each other. This 3D construction demands a novel approach to efficient analysis that allows for a more general overview without sacrificing the details of individual memory cells. The authors explore how to achieve this by identifying sources of variation and systematically parsing and manipulating the data file into smaller files. This methodology enables straightforward visualization of parametric variability in relation to test and process conditions and facilitating the creation of accessible documentation for future reference. The use of Python provides an open-source and user-friendly interface that can be further customized to enhance consistency and reusability.

articleTitle: BEOL Dielectric Film Delamination Reliability Improvement by Eliminating Silicon-Rich Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Fluorinated silica glass (FSG) has been widely used as an intermetal dielectric (IMD) due to its low dielectric constant (low k) and is normally deposited by a two-step process. This process consists of a high-density plasma (HDP) FSG layer for gap-fill, followed by a plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) FSG layer for planarization and as an IMD. The interface between these two films plays an important role in film property and stability. A silicon-rich layer at the interface of the two layers can cause an adhesion issue which can lead to film delamination during subsequent thermal cycles. This is a serious reliability problem for the wafer fabrication process. This paper focuses on the effect of the silane (SiH4) gas flow rate when switching from HDP to PECVD and its effect on the interface layer properties. Experiments were carried out with multiple recipe conditions of varying delays in switching the silane gas flow. Inline measurement of goodness of fit (GOF) and failure analysis (FA) data were collected for analysis. A shorter delay for the silane gas flow ramp during recipe switching formed a silicon-rich layer at the interface, which causes delamination. A perfect SiO2 interface with no silicon-rich layer is observed for a delay of 5sec or more, which is desirable for good film properties and wafer quality. This finding can be applied to improve adhesion and reliability on other processes such as IMD liner or STI HDP liner where a non-homogeneous film stack is formed by switching silane gas flow rate.

articleTitle: Using BERT Pre-Trained Image Transformers to Identify Potential Parametric Wafer Map Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Identifying defect patterns in wafer maps during manufacturing is vital for root cause analysis, enhancing foundry yields, and preventing returned material authorizations (RMA) in corporations. This paper introduces a novel self-supervised visual representation model christened BEIT-short for Bidirectional Encoder Representation from Image Transformers. The methodology we propose employs BEIT in conjunction with Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise to probe potential anomalies in parametric wafer maps, facilitating early identification and prevention of RMA incidents. Over a span of six months, our approach yielded a notable contraction in RMA instances and warded off a financial loss amounting to $9M USD. These commendable outcomes serve as robust testimony to the proficiency of our method; it pinpointed 35 prevailing complications within our company's product line with 99% accuracy and 83% precision.

articleTitle: Micro- and Macro-domain Analysis of Whole Silicon Carbide Wafers by T-ray Imaging: AM: Advanced Metrology
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper describes cameraless T-ray imaging of whole silicon carbide (SiC) wafers to reveal intricate patterns not seen before. Both the reflection mode and transmission mode T-ray imaging were conducted. The T-ray reflection mode image complements the features observed from the transmission mode with an opposite phase but with unparallel clarity that are not available from any other technique. Such clarity allows one to interpret the observed features in terms of the crystal growth process parameters and offers insights for improvement. The observed patterns are presumably due to the macro- and micro-domain formation in the boule during the crystal growth via seeded sublimation deposition process. It is presumed that the domain patterns were retained in the individual wafers even after the boule was sliced and polished to obtain each of those wafers. In addition, high resolution images were also taken from selected areas of a different wafer having epitaxial layer, via the same T-ray technique. The results are discussed in terms of the generated images and the crystal growing process.

articleTitle: Understanding DRAM Array Contact Missing: Mechanisms Study with Practical Solutions: YE: Yield Enhancement/Learnin
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Gaining insight into the interaction of processing elements is crucial for maintaining stability in device and electrical performances, particularly in high-volume manufacturing environment. This paper unveils a challenge arising during the transition from a hard mask process to a new vendor, leading to a run-to-run shift in the downstream dry etch process and causing under-etching. The study addresses this issue through the optimization of run-to-run processes, ensuring better alignment of hard mask film characteristics, and enhancement in within-wafer uniformity. Additionally, the paper endeavors to unravel the underlying process elements contributing to the occurrence of missing contacts.

articleTitle: Improvement on the Gate Oxide Integrity Caused by the TUB Charges in SOI Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Silicon-On-Insulator (SOI) technology is fabricated on substrate with Buried OXide layer (BOX). It offers high performance for noise and power consumption with high device density. This paper describes the journey of understanding and improving the Gate Oxide Integrity (GOI) for SOI technology. Investigation shows a strong influence from the charges within a TUB to the GOI performance. The TUB is a WELL region formed by Deep Trench Isolation (DTI) and the BOX layer. The TUB charges are influenced by the processes in the ONO (Oxide- Nitride-Oxide) process loop. The charges affect the surface bonding which defines the surface wettability and hence the cleaning efficiency. Using O2 plasma treatment to modify the surface bonding is proven to improve the GOI performance.

articleTitle: Wafer Edge RF LNR Yield Improvement in Oxide Etch Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In this paper, we are introducing a New Design Hot Edge Ring (NHER) to improve wafer edge yield. Lower yield at wafer edge has been a well-known phenomenon in wafer fabrication. Smaller die devices (typically more than 30K per wafer) are particularly susceptible to this phenomenon. Wafer yield is one, if not the most critical metric for wafer manufacturers and a few factors contribute to it, including defects, under/over etch and poor edge rounding. Hot Edge Ring (HER), a typical process kit used in Oxide chambers, serves to provide a buffer zone around the wafer, prevent cracks and defects from propagating to the edge, improves edge rounding and helps focus plasma onto the wafer. From our study, we found that by optimizing the thickness of the HER, wafer edge yield can be improved by 2% to 3%.

articleTitle: Reduction of Stiction Using Different Surface Treatment Methods on Elastomers and Their Longevity Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This study evaluated the effectiveness of Seal-Glide® surface treatments in reducing stiction of fluoroelastomer (FKM) and perfluoroelastomer (FFKM) O-rings to metal and quartz counter surfaces, which are commonplace in semiconductor industry applications. In these industries, removal of a stuck seal and its residues is associated with a significant downtime and labor cost. Therefore, minimizing the stiction have utmost importance to wafer output yield. Single-cycle tests simulated static operating conditions, whilst multi-cycle tests represented dynamic applications. Untreated O-rings exhibited significant stiction to aluminum and stainless steel in static conditions, potentially leading to seal adhesion and residue concerns. All tested surface treatments significantly reduced stiction to these metals. FFKMs generally showed an inherently lower stiction to quartz, and surface treatment offered a smaller but still significant further reduction in stiction. Multi-cycle tests measured far lower stiction forces compared to static tests, highlighting the dependence of O-ring stiction on compression time. FFKM4, exhibiting inherently higher stiction, benefitted most from surface treatments, which maintained their effectiveness even after 1000 cycles. SEM analysis suggested different mechanisms for stiction reduction depending on the surface topography and chemistry modification offered by each treatment method. This study demonstrates the potential of surface treatments to eliminate stiction concerns for a variety of fluoroelastomer and perfluoroelastomer O-rings in both static and dynamic semiconductor applications.

articleTitle: Highly Selective Si vs. SiGe and SiGe vs. Ge Wet Etch for Sub 2nm Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Selective Silicon (Si) and Silicon-Germanium (SiGe) etch chemistries have been developed to provide superior Si vs. SiGe and SiGe vs. Ge etch selectivity up to 1,000 or more. Unique etch differentiators demonstrate preferential etch suppressions of SiGe or Ge respectively. Another oxidative alkaline chemistry provides simultaneous Si and SiGe FinFET fin trimming in the range of 0.75-0.90. Their etch mechanisms and substrate compatibility are discussed.

articleTitle: Investigation of Power-Down Leakage Bin Fallout Caused by Fixed Location Gate Oxide Pin Hole
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The paper investigates power-down leakage bin failures attributed to a fixed-location gate oxide pinhole, consistently observed approximately 120mm away from the top corner of the Shallow Trench Isolation (STI). Through Finite Element Method (FEM)-based stress simulation, the study examines the high-stress area within the silicon active region. Inline investigation reveals a correlation between this stress-induced gate oxide pinhole and the annual Preventive Maintenance (PM) of a specific liner oxide furnace tool. Notably, a cracking line is identified on the SIC liner of the problematic tool. Suspicions arise regarding the non-uniform heat distribution on the processing wafer, leading to an escalation in within-wafer temperature gradient and thermal stress. Furthermore, the interaction between the liner oxide and the High-Density Plasma (HDP) oxide etch in the STI process loop is discussed as a potential factor contributing to heightened stress levels.

articleTitle: Optimization of Scatterometry Measurements by Enhancing with Machine Learning AM: Advanced Metrology
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In this study, we introduce a machine learning approach designed to augment the conventional Rigorous Coupled-Wave Analysis (RCWA) method used in scatterometry measurements. The utility of this approach is illustrated through two practical examples. Initially, we applied it to a recess structure in trench MOSFET. Following the application of our machine learning method to the RCWA model, the recess depth measurement exhibited improved stability and uniformity across the wafer. In the second example, we measured a 2D line trench in silicon (with a depth of 22 µm); here, both the top and bottom widths are parameters of interest. We show that our machine learning based model is more robust compared to the conventional RCWA method. Our results were then cross-verified using atomic force microscopy results and cross-section Scanning Electron Microscopy data, respectively.

articleTitle: Novel Approach Utilizing APIMS Technology for Analyzing CO & H2 Impurities in Semiconductor UHP Gases: AM: Advanced Metrology
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: New techniques for instrumentation setup and mathematical calibrations have been developed for Atmospheric Pressure Ionization Mass Spectrometers (APIMS) pertaining specifically to the measurements of carbon monoxide and hydrogen impurities in semiconductor UHP bulk gas. This has led to improved detection limits and measurement accuracies of these impurities. Verification of sub-ppb levels of these impurities in semiconductor bulk gases results in increased yields for wafer production.

articleTitle: Optimization of Area Selective Barrier on Different Metal Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Area selective atomic layer deposition of barriers with self-assembled monolayer (SAM) is increasingly being used in device fabrication to lower resistivity between inter layer metal interconnects by eliminating the barrier between them. In this paper, selectivity of atomic layer deposition (ALD) TaN on a Cu metal surface is optimized by tuning deposition conditions of both the SAM blocking layer and ALD TaN. Furthermore, we investigate SAM selectivity performance on different metal surfaces: Co, and Ru. The selectivity efficacy of SAM is shown to be highly dependent on deposition conditions.

articleTitle: Leveraging the Data Continuum for Advanced Root Cause Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: As semiconductor processing has developed and become increasingly complex over time, the amount of data and sources of data have also increased. This trend complicates the data analysis tasks performed by many fab engineers throughout the industry, requiring the need to gather data from multiple sources and reach conclusions quickly and efficiently. In the case of root cause analysis for a deviation or excursion, it is especially important for analysis solutions to pinpoint possible root causes quickly and allow the engineer to contain and resolve the issue before it becomes a major quality incident. Today, there are effective solutions to address some of these cases. However, more advanced and automated analysis solutions are needed to unlock interactivity across the full data continuum not only within the fab, but across the life cycle of the device. One approach, which is used by the new Fab.da solution provided by Synopsys, organizes the individual data components into a data lakehouse, demonstrates performance improvements when compared to older technologies, and unlocks new use cases in the areas of decision support and joining with data from the design and mask optimization space.

articleTitle: Analyzing Time-Dependent Behavior of Wafer Outgassing in the Front Opening Unified Pod
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Quantitative analysis of remaining reaction byproducts from wafer processing can indicate sensitivity of patterning processes against humidity and sitting time, and suggest subsequent method for preventing manufacturing failure. However, due to its inherent nature of wafer outgassing, obtaining quantitative information with controlled standard deviation is highly challenging. In this study, we adopt 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> order ordinary differential equation to interpret time-dependent wafer outgassing profile in the Front Opening Unified Pod (FOUP) using in-line measurement tool, and thereby derive outgassing rate. Compared with the previous method, the calculated outgassing rate showed reduced deviation between samples, by approximately 21.0%.

articleTitle: Solution for Pond Shape Defect Near Wafer Edge
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Defect reduction is one of the key factors to improve the process stability and yield in lithography process. This paper discusses defects in pond shape around wafer edge. These defects have mild surface topography difference on photoresist. Majority of the defects exist on the wafer edge area where there is Wafer Edge Exposure (WEE). This paper discusses the defect mechanism and potential solution for this defect type. ASML I-line Scanner and TEL track were used in this test. Investigation was carried out on the defect formation on same type of photoresist with different recipe content. Results indicated that recipe with small WEE size and without chemical EBR tends to induce this pond defects; total defect quantity is related to softbake & WEE condition. Based on the elemental analysis and Design of experiment (DOE), we can conclude that pond defect is generated where nitrogen popping or foaming as a side product of the photoreaction of DNQ-based resists during exposure. By optimizing softbake, WEE and recipe structure this pond defect could be eliminated.

articleTitle: Sustainability Model for Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Sustainability is becoming more challenging for semiconductor industry as the size of foundries and complexity of wafer fabrication increase<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1], [2]</sup>. When we look at the commercial and sustainability side of semiconductor manufacturing, we need to define methods and indicators to measure both. This paper describes a method and model to measure the efficiency for any semiconductor process step. With this model, it is possible to compare, track, and benchmark the sustainability characteristic of a manufacturing process step and flow overall.

articleTitle: Streamlining Critical Queue Timer Management: A Digital Twin Approach to Optimize Frontend Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In semiconductor frontend manufacturing, critical queue timers are considered to avoid costly rework and scrap, making it an important objective to address in production planning and control. We showcase our planning approach, a multi-objective hybrid planning model embedded into a digital twin, and compare its results against classical dispatching schemes.
