By varying the weighting for each individual optimization objective, we analyze to what extent time constraint violations can be minimized under the consideration of balanced production targets. The paper ends with a demonstration of our key findings and remaining research topics.

articleTitle: Novel Chemical Development for Post Metal Etch Clean
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Advanced semiconductor manufacturing requires use of large amounts of environmentally toxic chemicals to process wafers. With advancement of technology node, demand for new chemical developments and associated risk to environment is ever increasing. In this paper, we present the development of new cleaning formulation for Back-End-of-Line post metal etch cleaning where the use of azole, a toxic chemical component, is drastically reduced. We implemented this new, environmentally friendly formulation in high volume manufacturing and achieved a cleaning efficiency and device performance comparable to the process of record formulation.

articleTitle: Q-time Assessment on Electroplated Nickel/Gold Interface Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper investigated the interface quality of electroplated nickel (Ni) and gold (Au) layers processed at different Q-time. This study is important for semiconductor manufacturing processes because Q-time between Ni and Au plating is sometimes inevitable and maintaining good plating quality is essential. It was found that more than 24hours of waiting time between Ni and Au plating did not impact the Ni/Au interface's quality.

articleTitle: Water Vapor Measurements of Ultra-Pure Gases for Critical Manufacturing Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents how to characterize an industrial trace moisture transmitter and a summary of an anonymous characterization of transmitters from different brands. Measurement results indicate significant deviation in results between the transmitters indicating significant differences in their measurement performance. Therefore, knowledge of how to characterize a trace moisture transmitter enables choosing optimal instrumentation, and thus improves the process where the gas is used and measured.

articleTitle: Analyses of eSiGe Defects Induced by Outdoor Airborne Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: A comprehensive investigation was conducted with the goal of measuring the impact of outdoor airborne nanoparticles on defect generation during the manufacturing process. During periods of elevated airborne particle levels and increased occurrences of eSiGe (embedded Silicon-Germanium) defects, experimental bare wafers were employed to collect airborne particles. The examination of defect counts facilitated the confirmation of the sources of defects. Given the complex web of factors influencing defects within the manufacturing environment, a sophisticated data processing algorithm was developed to pinpoint the specific role of nanoparticles in the total count of defect particles within a single, particle-sensitive manufacturing step. In this pilot-scale study, outdoor nano contamination affected a total of 13 out of 120 data collection days across three different fabrication sites, leading to overgrowth defects in the embedded Si-Ge process. The unique aspect of this study involves explaining the influence of outdoor nanoparticles on eSiGe defects using both a short-term experimental method and a long-term inline data science approach.

articleTitle: Accelerating Chamber-to-Chamber Matching Using AI
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: A critical challenge in the high-yield manufacturing of semiconductor devices is deploying a developed manufacturing process across multiple chambers, tools, or plants to scale up production. Due to inherent tool variability, the same process settings can lead to variations in process outcomes across chambers or tools. Currently, chamber or tool matching is commonly performed experimentally, leading to considerable additional deployment costs. The following case study showcases an AI- based methodology to accelerate chamber variability and yield optimization during typical semiconductor manufacturing workflows. An optimal set of process conditions that maximize across- wafer yield and meet recipe targets is first identified for a baseline chamber. It is then shown how to match the recipe to additional chambers, accounting for variability between them and ensuring consistent process outcomes. The presented methodology requires minimal experimental effort, thereby greatly reducing process development time and cost. The results illustrate the application of this methodology across four distinct processing chambers, underscoring its versatility and efficacy.

articleTitle: Innovative Approaches for 3D Metrology and Defect Analysis on Advanced Packaging Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: With the rapid growth of advanced packaging technology, the task of conducting metrology and defect analysis on new packaging structures becomes more complex and demanding. This paper will present innovative approaches for conducting three-dimensional (3D) metrology and defect analysis on a high bandwidth memory (HBM) structure using a wafer-level plasma focused ion beam (PFIB) and scanning electron microscope (SEM) DualBeam system.

articleTitle: Selective Auto-Labeling for Deep Learning-Based Domain-Specific Image Classification in Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In the realm of semiconductor process control, the rapid and accurate identification of issues through historical equipment maintenance imagery is crucial for timely corrective actions. However, the application of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image classification within this domain is hampered by the scarcity of labeled data, a consequence of the highly specialized and complex nature of semiconductor manufacturing processes. This paper introduces a novel approach to mitigate the challenge of minimal labeling by implementing a confidence-based auto-labeler. Leveraging domain-specific knowledge and a minimal set of 13 labeled images, we successfully generate a sufficiently large and reliable labeled dataset. This dataset serves as the foundation for training CNN-based models, demonstrating the potential for significant improvements in decision-making efficiency in semiconductor process control. Our methodology not only addresses the labeling bottleneck but also sets a precedent for employing machine learning and AI in enhancing the robustness of semiconductor manufacturing and maintenance practices.

articleTitle: Wafer Substrate Bevel Significance to Edge Yield Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In the realm of semiconductor technology, the pursuit of higher wafer yield has driven researchers to focus on optimizing wafer edge performance. This paper delves into the relationship between localized four-corner edge yield loss and substrate characteristics, with a specific emphasis on the substrate bevels. In this study, we utilized p-(1 0 0) 200nm wafers sourced from various vendors, with a particular spotlight on a substrate that employs alkaline etching, in contrast to the acid etching used by others. Studies show that after alkaline etching, the (1 0 0) surface exhibits smoother characteristics compared to (1 1 0), posing challenges in particle and film residue adhesion. Furthermore, longer bevels in the specific substrate, resulting in heightened particle adhesion, film wrap-around, and peeling could contribute to defectivity. This intricate interplay between the substrate etching process and bevel length emerges as a significant factor in four-corner edge yield loss investigation. Through experimentation, this study demonstrates an approximate 30% yield improvement in the split lots performed. Overall, this research underscores the paramount importance of reducing defect density at the wafer edge. It sheds light on potential strategies for enhancing wafer yield and product quality in semiconductor manufacturing.

articleTitle: MTP Data Retention Improvement by Salicide Clean Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Data retention failure is a serious reliability concern for logic embedded non-volatile memory (eNVM) in multiple-time-programming (MTP) applications. Data retention represents the ability of the memory cells to maintain the data state over a long period of time. One of the root causes for MTP data retention degradation is high induced charges generated during the wafer processing. Under thermal activation (bake test), these charges are likely to be displaced and attract the electrons from floating gate (FG) causing the drop in MTP cell current. Unlike the one-time-programming (OTP) application, MTP cell architecture does not have a salicide block oxide (SAB) which works as FG shielding layer. Thus, any process step with high induced charges before contact etch stop layer (CESL) might cause major data retention issue. In this work, we will discuss in detail on how does salicide clean induces charges on wafer and affects data retention degradation in 0.18um process. We also demonstrated that MTP data retention and circuit probing (CP) yield significantly improves by introducing CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>De-ionized (DI) wafer during salicide clean to reduce the friction induced charges.

articleTitle: Evaluation of different metal preclean conditions for MOL for 2nm and beyond: Topic/category: AEPM : Advanced Equipment Processes and Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: We report the results from evaluating different metal preclean conditions for MOL applications for 2nm and beyond. Two different chambers were evaluated for removal of metal interfacial oxide prior to MOL metal liner deposition. Different blanket oxide etch experiments were conducted with heated H2 plasma and H2 plasma combined with Ar sputter removal (2-in-1 process) to understand etch removal, uniformity. Further electrical performance on MOL test structure was done to evaluate which preclean process showed superior electrical yield.

articleTitle: Optimization of FINFET Single Diffusion Break Structure Profile
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: FIN recess profile of single diffusion break devices is optimized to resolve one of the middle of line challenges- unlanded trench silicide. Results show improvement in wafer edge yield, particularly for that of small die products. Alongside with yield improvement, e-beam defect inspection was fine tuned to detect such defects in the logic area early in the line, as soon as middle of line (MOL) contacts were fabricated. All these developments help to lower wafer scraps at the end of line and to improve fab economy.

articleTitle: Big Data Analytics for Real Time Dispatch
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing industry is leading industry in generating large volume of data because of its complexities of processes and automated nature. It not only produces data in big volume but in an immense variety of formats at a rapid pace through various components in a semiconductor manufacturing facility (Fab). Real Time Dispatch (RTD) is a component in the automated fab which takes decisions to dispatch lots to tools in real time. It generates tons of dispatching data. Traditional database management system is not able to manage such volume and variety of data. This study will present a solution or framework to collect, store and retrieve real time dispatch data efficiently in a semiconductor fab and utilize it for the improvement of fab operations. This is important because dispatching data can be used in many ways to improve dispatching rules and algorithms for tools, troubleshoot undesirable dispatching decisions quickly and easily and measure and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) for tools and the fab.

articleTitle: Study of Wafer Arcing Defects on PECVD Low Deposition Rate TEOS Oxide Thin Film
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In this study, we have investigated wafer arcing defects on low deposition rate oxide thin film using tetraethyl-orthosilicate (TEOS) by Plasma Enhanced Chemical Vapor Deposition (PECVD). During the experiments, we considered process parameters such as the O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/TEOS gas flow ratio, RF power, and hardware configurations. A proposed mechanism for the formation of wafer arcing defects has been put forward. A process condition was found to eliminate wafer arcing defects while maintaining thin film properties.

articleTitle: Metal Mask Rework Optimization for Metal with TaN Precision Resistor on it
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In 0.18um CMOS designs, the choice of resistor materials commonly includes polysilicon and substrate well. While these materials serve their purpose, traditional silicon resistors are known to exhibit a high-temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR), which can introduce undesirable variations in performance under different temperature conditions. To counter this limitation and ensure robust performance across a range of operating temperatures, TaN thin film resistors are introduced into the metal loops of CMOS circuits. The paper investigates metal line short failures in Metal-6, particularly focusing on wafers undergoing photoresist rework. Notably, Metal-6 incorporates an additional TaN module compared to other inter-metal layers. This inclusion necessitates a thermal process with temperatures lower than the critical point of copper phase change. Consequently, this lower-temperature process increases the likelihood of copper precipitation, where copper is added to aluminum to minimize migrations. However, copper precipitation can result in the hardening of AlCu metal, making it challenging to etch through completely. To address the metal line short issue, the paper proposes a solution involving the replacement of the photoresist rework tool with a type-B tool featuring a lower-temperature platen. This adjustment helps mitigate the effects of copper precipitation, thereby reducing the occurrence of metal line short failures in Metal-6.

articleTitle: Elimination of Passivation RIE Arcing in RFSOI Process
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper will demonstrate the method to resolve the plasma-induced damage (PID) at Wafer ID area, i.e., Optical Character Recognition (OCR) region arcing on silicon- on-insulator (SOI) wafer of RFSOI passivation reactive-ion etching (RIE) process. This is important because the arcing phenomenon causes manufacturing cycle time delay due to Wafer ID reading failure, as well as yield loss on dies near the arcing region. The study was designed by allowing the photolithography exposure followed by develop process at the OCR region during the Top Metal, passivation, and Aluminum (Al) masks to get rid of the floating Al at that region. The result showed 0% arcing was achieved even with high passivation RIE RF bias power. The power of the laser scribe process has also been optimized in order to compensate Wafer ID readability issue at OSAT after the implementation of new process scheme.

articleTitle: Rapid Thermal Annealing for Shallow Junction and its Impact on FinFET Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Millisecond annealing (MSA) achieves increased dopant activation and suppresses short-channel effects after junction implantations. In this paper, we will explore ways to optimize conventional spike anneal processes on dopants activation management.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based SEM Image Analysis for Automatic Detection and Classification of Wafer Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: A machine learning (ML) based approach is proposed for analyzing Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) images and classifying review defects. Accurate and timely SEM image analysis is crucial and impacts manufacturing yield. The state-of-the-art object detection model YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once version 8) is used as it offers a good balance between accuracy and inference speed. This work demonstrates the utility of YOLO for SEM ADC and extends capability using ensemble voting to achieve higher quality results.

articleTitle: Dynamic Time Warping Constraints for Semiconductor Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: We present a new method for preprocessing semiconductor fabrication sensor signals that improves fault detection model performance. Machine learning has allowed for advances in fault detection and classification, but there are still difficulties in applying these techniques to the monitoring of fabrication processes when some variation in processing time is acceptable. The new method uses domain knowledge - specifically, process recipe steps - to create constraints that better align signals along the time dimension, which addresses this problem of nonlinear siznalaliznment,

articleTitle: Process Margin Improvement and Cost Saving from a New Plasma Oxide Etch Process with Endpoint Algorithm During Photolithography Positive- to Negative-Tone Develop Conversion
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: A DRAM contact oxide dry etch process had severe yield loss and inline parameter deviation when the photo process was changed from legacy positive tone develop (PTD) to negative tone develop (NTD) for cost saving. A new contact oxide etch with a new peak and valley algorithm has been developed to improve the process margin by >50% depth of focus (DOF). The results from the implementation of this new contact etch process together with the PTD to NTD conversion improve the contact oxide etch process window for better chamber to chamber matching and inline critical dimension (CD) uniformity.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Process Optimization for EUV MOR: Equipment Trace Data Feature Extraction and Machine Learning is Essential for CD Control
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: We explore the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to enhance lithography processes involving metal-oxide resists (MOR) for Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography. Through a systematic experimental approach, we investigate the impact of lithography processes and 120 equipment parameters on critical metrology features such as Critical Dimension (CD) Mean and CD Standard Deviation (Std) to accelerate the development of this technology into the industry. Our findings reveal clear insights between experimental settings and metrology outcomes, highlighting the significance of lithography parameter variability and control. Additionally, we uncovered valuable insights into the correlation between sensor-trace features and experimental perturbations, paving the way for enhanced process control and optimization. This collaborative effort underscores the importance of leveraging purpose-built AI platforms and Data Science to drive further continuous improvements in high volume semiconductor manufacturing and research and development pilot lines.

articleTitle: The Value of In-Line Metrology for Advanced Process Control: AM: Advanced Metrology
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In-line metrology provides critical information for feedback and feedforward process control. In high-volume manufacturing, the fundamental question is: how fast, how frequent, and how accurate measurements should be made to satisfy control requirements. This paper develops a framework to study the tradeoff among the sampling rate, the delay, and the quality of measurements and the effect of these canonical factors on the variability of processes. As a consequence of this fundamental tradeoff, the relative value of virtual metrology with respect to real metrology can be quantified in the context of advanced process control.

articleTitle: A Noble Cause: Reduction of Ne and Xe Consumption for Gas Laser Mixtures: MS: Manufacturing for Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The work presents a case study describing how the laser gas lifetime of excimer laser based ultra-short laser thermal anneal (LTA) tool can be extended by spiking of the marginal gas component. A reduction of Xenon and Neon consumption and the related costs by approximately 75% was reached. To investigate the degradation mechanism of the laser gas, a residual gas analyzer (RGA) study was performed. Subsequently the process window for the laser parameters cavity pressure and gas composition was evaluated using a design of experiment (DoE) study. The influence of these laser cavity settings on the output parameters maximum reachable energy and pulse duration was investigated.

articleTitle: Supporting Fab Operations Using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Over recent years semiconductor operations have grown in scope, dynamics, and complexity and consequently advanced scheduling algorithms and manufacturing engineers can no longer quickly estimate the best performing schedule. In this paper we present how machine learning, in real time, can be used to augment and support manufacturing engineers. The presented results, obtained from production deployments, show that AI assisted scheduling can improve Key Performance Indicators by, on average, over 2% with little to no downside.

articleTitle: Method to Control Polymer Generation During Thick Top Metal Process to Reduce Sidewall Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to control sidewall polymer coverage generated during thick top metal etch by implementing a reticle transmission (RT) cut-off at both the masking and the metal etch stages. This is achieved by adjusting the photoresist thickness as well as the etch recipe chemistry. This comprehensive strategy aims to enhance device performance, reduce manufacturing complexities, and improve the overall process yield. Furthermore, the compatibility of this approach with existing manufacturing processes minimizes the need for extensive process modifications or investments into new equipment.

articleTitle: NVM Tunnel Oxide Integration in an Advanced BCD Node and its Impact on GOI
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents the options to integrate tunnel oxide (TOX) in an advanced node Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (BCD) process and compare their impact on the GOI of TOX. In the case of using silicon nitride a protection layer and Hot phosphoric acid etches (HotPhos) process for its removal, we study its effects to TOX in terms of residual Phosphorus, its clean-up method, and the resulting Gate Oxide Integrity (GOI) through Ramp-to-breakdown (Vbd) and Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) measurements. We find that HotPhos significantly degrades GOI and it's not due to the residual Phos it leaves in the shallow surface of TOX. SkinClean process is effective in residual Phosphorus removal but not helpful for GOI improvement.

articleTitle: Real-time etching process monitoring and end-point detection with a time-of-flight mass spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This study shows the capabilities of a time-of-flight mass spectrometer to monitor etching processes in real time. The experiments described in this work involve SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> etching using CHF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> gases, and the results demonstrate the capability of the instrument to detect etching endpoints and track relevant species during the process.

articleTitle: Wafer Edge Unsalicided Poly Resistor Matching Optimization with Spike Anneal Temperature Control
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Rapid Thermal Processing (RTP) is widely used in the world of semiconductor manufacturing. A process which enables rapid heating of samples to high temperatures and capability to perform short processes for a required duration of time. The steep heating rates in the RTP systems are enabled by high intensity lamps through control by thermocouples and pyrometers. A good control of the cooling step must also be handled well to prevent dislocations or sample breakages. This signifies the importance that a good control of precise applied thermal budget is required. In this paper we uncover an improved Spike Anneal Edge Temperature tuning methodology and control to optimize wafer Edge Unsalicided P-Poly Resistor Matching. This tuning methodology relies on the creation of virtual cold zones to counteract the wafer edge steep temperature effect induced by different heat capacity between the wafer and edge ring. An ~80% Edge Yield Recovery was demonstrated after implementation of the improved Spike Anneal tuning Methodology and control.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Innovations for Sustainable Copper Management in Semiconductor Wastewater
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the potential of a High Efficiency Selective Electrochemical Cell (HESEC) to recover copper from a variety of semiconductor wastewater streams while also achieving EPA discharge compliance. The copper chemical-mechanical planarization (CuCMP), wet etch, and electroplating processes produce significant levels of copper laden wastewaters with complex matrices that make recovery of the copper difficult. Based on our experimental results, the HESEC provides insight into how novel electrochemical cell designs can be used to achieve selective copper removal and recovery from different wastewater streams and open up new possibilities for economical point source treatment and implementation of sustainable practices.

articleTitle: Method of Controlling Interface Oxide in Polysilicon Emitter PNP Bipolar Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Polysilicon is widely used as material for Emitter in vertical Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJT) to obtain high current gain (Beta). To optimize the electrical properties of polysilicon (Poly) Emitter BJTs, interface between the Emitter poly and the Base needs to be engineered carefully. This paper explains the sources and effects of interface oxide thickness variations in PNP transistors fabricated with polysilicon Emitter deposited by LPCVD furnaces. By growing a thin layer of chemical oxide at the interface prior to the deposition of polysilicon, a controllable, repeatable, and uniform layer of interface oxide is achieved, giving a stable and consistent electrical performance across all furnace boat positions.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Modeling and Machine Learning for Preventative Maintenance Prediction in Semiconductor Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Machinery within semiconductor manufacturing facilities exhibits high degrees of integration and complexity, making it susceptible to unexpected failures. These failures pose the risk of disrupting all manufacturing operations, indirectly impacting profit and overall production output. To avoid such problems, predictive models can be used to forecast the next tool state and anticipate tool failure. Using these predictions, preventative maintenance measures can take place to avoid such disruptions to the supply chain. This paper introduces two approaches for the preventative maintenance prediction problem, a probabilistic approach and a machine learning approach. The probabilistic approach leverages a Markov chain to model the probabilities for the set of outcomes given the current state of a tool. These probabilities are calculated by a conditional probability formula with historical data on each tool's past operational states. Additionally, the preventative maintenance prediction model is expanded to incorporate features from the semiconductor manufacturing plant to be used as input into machine learning algorithms. These additional features further refine the predictive capabilities of the preventative maintenance prediction model by improving model robustness.

articleTitle: Semiconductor Manufacturing Data Synthesis through GANs
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel application of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) in the creation of a digital twin of a semiconductor manufacturing plant, as well as the investigation of new evaluation metrics in synthetic data quality. Digital twins are the next technological step for long-term semiconductor manufacturing capacity planning, performance optimization, and job scheduling. However, real-time predictive analytics for this industry demands substantial historical data about equipment, operations, and performance metrics like Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE). In cases where such data is unavailable, GANs can fill these data gaps by providing sufficient synthetic data to enable predictive modeling and digital twin creation. This investigation successfully generated synthetic semiconductor manufacturing data through Conditional, Wasserstein, and Copula GANs, enabling the creation of the digital twin for predictive modeling and further research of manufacturing improvements. A new method of evaluating synthetic data through a metric based on the distance between distributions scaled by similarity is also investigated.

articleTitle: 3D Shape Measurements of Patterned Silicon Wafers
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Wave Front Phase Imaging (WFPI), a new technique that can measure the free form wafer shape of a patterned silicon wafer using only the intensity of the reflected light is presented. In the WFPI system, the wafer is held either horizontally or vertically, depending on the configuration of the optical system. The wave front phase is then measured by acquiring only the 2-dimensional intensity distribution of the reflected non-coherent light at two or more distances along the optical path using a digital imaging sensor. This method allows for very high data acquisition speed, equal to the camera's shutter time, and a high number of data points with the same number of pixels as available in the digital imaging sensor. In the measurements presented in this paper, we acquired 7.3 million data points on a full 200mm patterned silicon wafer with a lateral resolution of 65µm when the wafer was held vertically and 3.4 million data points on the system where the wafer was resting horizontally with a 96µm lateral resolution. The vertical system presented can also acquire data on a 300mm silicon wafer in which case 16.3 million data points with the same 65µm spatial resolution were collected.

articleTitle: The Digital Twin Difference - a Blueprint for the Semiconductor Manufacturing Metaverse
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The industrial metaverse broadly encompasses highly connected enterprises that seek to streamline multi-cloud or multi-source data and harvest the actionable insights it yields. The Digital Twin enables the virtual recreation of product life cycles from design to production so that expensive, critical, activities, like EDA testing, or Design simulation, can be conducted virtually before allocating expensive resources to this in the physical world. This solution is critical to the national dialog on regional chips manufacturing in geographies that are conducive for reasons of cost, technological capability, and last but not the least, aligned in business and national interest. However, the semiconductor production digital twin, and the metaverse it activates, must be differentiated to be of value to a high volume, high yield production environment. Compared to other industries that are more focused on challenges of assembly, quality inspection, and test scenarios for high performance electronics, devices, vehicles, semiconductor production spans a prolonged life cycle, from seed crystal to silicon to device.

articleTitle: In-house Test Wafer Reclaim for Fab Cost and Wastage Reduction: MS: Manufacturing for Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: In semiconductor fabrication facilities, non-production test wafers constitute a substantial amount of the non-equipment-related consumable expense. With the escalating demand and increased costs associated with bare silicon test wafers, as well as the limited viability of external reclamation, the imperative to extend the lifecycle of recycled wafers and establish an in-house reclamation process has become pronounced for major chip manufacturers. External reclaim usually comes with a higher cost per wafer and a limited recycle lifespan. In contrast, in-house reclaim offers a cost that is significantly lower, at only a fraction of the external reclaim cost per wafer, and provides a much longer recycle lifespan, making it a more cost-effective solution. Historically, Semiconductor fabs lacked the capability to recondition test wafers that had reached the end of their usable lifespan. Those silicon test wafers failed to reclaim global specification will be downgraded and directly outsourced to external vendors for reclaim once they are not able to meet the usable specifications. This paper's primary objective is to present an innovative approach that leverages existing in-house resources to develop a practical methodology for extending the lifespan of test wafers and providing a comprehensive reclamation solution. The recently developed in-house wafer reclamation process at Micron has significant yield improvements, met with the global reclaim specifications. Furthermore, a novel combination of new CMP (Chemical Mechanical Polishing) slurries and process optimization in both CMP and Wet processes has been devised and effectively applied to the reclamation process, achieving an impressive reclaim yield for high-volume operations. These advances have instilled confidence in in-house recycling and reclamation processes within semiconductor fabrication. While specific figures remain confidential, the results of this paper underscore the viability of in-house silicon wafer reclamation and elucidate a cost-effective, high-yield methodology. These insights are intended for dissemination as an innovative method to achieve hundreds of millions of dollars annualized network savings and significant wastage reduction.

articleTitle: Enabling 300 mm Wafer-Scale Fabrication of Superconducting Quantum Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: Superconducting quantum computing has demonstrated exponential improvements in coherence times over the past two decades, bringing us to the present Noisy Intermediate Scale Quantum (NISQ) era. Improvements in materials and fabrication techniques are still required along with circuit and algorithm innovations to move beyond the NISQ era. We discuss several aspects of the process development work that enables the fabrication of superconducting quantum devices and circuits at 300 mm wafer scale, using materials, processes and tools that are entirely compatible with high-volume integrated circuit fabs. Damascene structures of superconducting tantalum and aluminum (embedded in high resistivity silicon substrates) are described along with examples of process control. The use of such structures for coplanar waveguide resonators in quantum circuits is described, along with modifications to enable integration of normal metal traps to mitigate quasiparticle poisoning. This paper also includes a description of the considerable process development required to enable ALD-TaN based Josephson junctions fabricated with entirely 300 mm compatible processes, in contrast to the lift-off based processes currently in wide use for qubit fabrication. It concludes with a description of how these efforts help with establishing a Quantum Foundry at NY CREATES (a non-profit organization) that can democratize access to advanced qubit fabrication by offering an open superconducting quantum Process Design Kit (PDK).

articleTitle: Scatterometry Critical Dimension Solution for Gate All Around Sheet-Specific Metrology: Topic/category: Advanced Metrology
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: The complex vertically stacked gate-all-around (GAA) manufacturing process drives the demand for more challenging inline metrology requirements. GAA technology with specific technical requirements starts from the first process step, 1) The superlattice requires defect-free growth of multi-stack Si/SiGe pairs with matched thicknesses, %Ge per layer, sharp interfaces, and minimized thermal Ge diffusion. More critical steps, among others, are the 2) partial recess of the sacrificial SiGe layers that precede 3) the inner spacers which prevent a channel to source/drain short circuit and reduce the parasitic capacitance, and 4) the channel release process at the “remove poly gate” module, where the SiGe is selectively removed before the high-k metal gate. Driven by tight performance control, a sheet-specific metrology solution is highly desired at each of the above four critical steps. The ideal solution for such an application is non-destructive, precise, accurate, and highly productive. In this paper, a scatterometry critical dimension (SCD) solution for the GAA sheet-specific measurement from various GAA structures is presented. The SCD solution includes an advanced and optimized full Mueller Matrix spectroscopic ellipsometry in conjunction with a physics-assisted machine learning (ML) algorithm. Additionally, the best methodology to address the solution's robustness to process variation is described and presented. It will be shown that an optimized signal-to-noise ratio combined with ML can provide a superior optical metrology solution to the growing challenge in GAA applications.

articleTitle: Coming of Age in Computational SEM
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: For almost three decades, SEM (scanning electron microscopy) systems have been the main workhorse of CD metrology for advanced semiconductor nodes. While we have achieved a basic understanding of a SEM system's general behaviors for analyzing many sample types and applications, the systematic selection of SEM signal parameters with respect to all the varying parameters in both tool and sample has been elusive. Computational SEM, a quantitatively informed simulation approach to optimization of the output SEM signals, is a more precise and crucial approach to modern characterization. Several application studies will be shown in this work as examples of how computational SEM can be applied to many different practical fab SEM measurement situations. The first two involve HV-SEM, which has recently become a mainstream fab tool for measurement of HAR holes and trenches in VNAND lines, and HV-SEM which is currently using see-through SEM imaging to detect the bottom layer registration to calibrate overlay. Such work is time-consuming and expensive in terms of tool time, and such solutions are very dependent on the exact measurement situation; simulation support for such roles can save much tool time, achieve more conclusive results, and avoid confusion resulting from experimentation using poorly characterized samples. Another case will apply HV-SEM to see-thru imaging of buried copper gratings, of interest for overlay. A last case study will apply computational methods to demonstrate how the DI-SEM detection of different defects in an advanced ONO stack can help to estimate how signal to noise ratios (SNR) are affected by choice of DI-SEM beam conditions. DOE (design of experiments) SEM simulation studies concerning these different cases will be performed using SimuSEM software based on NIST's JMONSEL [1]–[4] which is a first-principles Monte Carlo electron scattering physics engine that has been well validated for over ten years as quantitatively accurate. AMAG SimuSEM, with a user-friendly GUI version, [5]–[6] makes JMONSEL usable and mass-producible by converting it into a virtual tool calculator, a computational SEM with DOE capabilities. This work will also demonstrate the quantitative accuracy of the model solutions, comparing simulated results to real HV-SEM images of HAR holes. The work will conclude with quantitative results of HAR Hole and VNAND HV-SEM, HV-SEM imaging of buried copper gratings, and defects in an ONO stack that demonstrate the importance of computational SEM for improving SEM usefulness, productivity, and value for future SEM applications in-line.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Sort Job Optimization for Wafer Bonding Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: This paper presents a solution to optimally create a grouping of wafers that are to be bonded with each other at a wafer bonding tool. Wafer bonding requires a source/top wafer to be flipped over and aligned over a target/bottom wafer for bonding. Therefore, a pair of FOUPs carrying the same number of top and bottom wafers, respectively, needs to be created. This is particularly challenging when wafers arrive to their bonding step in FOUPs of varying wafer counts. That could require executing multiple runs at the sorter tool to combine wafers into the two needed FOUPS of equal wafer count for each group. Depending on a fab's momentary business priorities and capacity constraints, different performance measures are critical for such a grouping decision: Higher throughput for the wafer bonding process and its downstream operations as driven by larger bonding groups, higher compliance for given preferences guiding the particular wafer-to-wafer pairing, capacity conflicts due to higher sorter workload, and individual lot cycle time delays due to non-value-added sort operations establish partly opposing objectives. This paper proposes an algorithm that continuously decides bonding groups in compliance with a rolling-horizon-consistent trade-off configuration for operationally meaningful objectives.

articleTitle: New High Resolution Method to Characterize CMP Slurry Particle Size Distributions
publicationTitle: 2024 35th Annual SEMI Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing Conference (ASMC)
abstract: A new method has been created to more easily and accurately measure particle size distributions (PSD) in Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) slurries from a few nanometers to one micrometer in size. It combines the use of a newly developed nanoparticle atomizer (NPA) and a Scanning Mobility Particle Sizer (SMPS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup>), and requires only uncomplicated process steps of dilution and injection. This new method provides a straightforward means of assessing slurry characteristics even down to nanometer-sized particles, which are now being used in the semiconductor industry with increasing frequency. Such measurements enable improved qualification of outgoing or incoming slurries, the opportunity for better monitoring and control of CMP parameters (in process development, or in-line) to reduce defects and waste, as well as to monitor slurry aging.
